mainTopic: The laws of אונאה: time limits for buyer and seller, sales by a בעל הבית, merchants, and conditions that waive the claim
overview: This amud deals with אונאה, selling at an unfair price. First the גמרא asks whether a מוכר who was cheated has the same short time to back out as a לוקח. A proof from the merchants of לוד is pushed aside, and then רב נחמן rules that a מוכר can always back out, because he no longer holds the item to check its price. Next, רבא and רב חסדא rule that a buyer who buys a בעל הבית's personal belongings has no claim of אונאה, because people charge extra for things they care about. A new משנה then teaches that both buyer and seller are protected, and that the cheated side may choose to cancel the sale or get the difference back. The גמרא brings the פסוק for this and explains why the Torah had to mention both sides. It then explains רבי יהודה's view that a תגר has no אונאה, and asks whose opinion the משנה follows, concluding that it is רבי יהודה הנשיא. Finally, רב and שמואל argue about a sale made on condition that there is no אונאה claim, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: That is why the merchants went back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its explanation of the תגרי לוד story: if a מוכר can always back out, that explains why the merchants went back to the רבנן's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is because of this that they went back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof that started just before this line. It says the merchants' change of heart makes sense if a מוכר can always back out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The merchants of לוד were sellers. רבי טרפון's ruling gave buyers more time to back out, and that only hurt the merchants. If sellers can back out at any time anyway, the longer window gave the merchants nothing in return. So it makes sense that they went back to the רבנן's shorter time limit.

keyTerms.meaning: They went back (here: the merchants went back to following the רבנן)
Because of this

phrases.english: It is because of this that they went back.
phrases.notes: "They" are the merchants of לוד, who first liked רבי טרפון's ruling and then went back to the view of the רבנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי חָזְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the proof that began before this section, which assumes a מוכר can always back out.
steps.raayaObject: That a מוכר may always back out of a sale with אונאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the תגרי לוד going back to the view of the רבנן after רבי טרפון extended the time limit

steps.title: If the seller had the same limit, the merchants would gain nothing by going back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the proof: if a מוכר had the same short window as a לוקח, the merchants would have had no reason to go back.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say a seller is also like a buyer, what difference would it make to them? Just as the Sages made a fix for the buyer, they also made a fix for the seller!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the proof stronger by testing the opposite view. If a מוכר has the same time limit as a לוקח, the merchants' change of heart does not make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both sides get the same window, then רבי טרפון's longer window would help the merchants as sellers just as much as it hurt them as buyers' counterparts. So they would have no reason to complain and go back. That suggests the time limit must apply only to a לוקח.

keyTerms.meaning: Seller
Buyer
Is treated like a buyer
What difference does it make to them?
A fix or rule the רבנן made to protect someone

phrases.english: But if you say
that a seller is also treated like a buyer,
what difference does it make to them?
Just as the Sages made
a fix for the buyer,
so too the Sages made
a fix for the seller!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ מוֹכֵר נָמֵי כְּלוֹקֵחַ דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 1 by showing that the opposite view cannot explain the merchants' behavior.
steps.raayaObject: That only a לוקח has a time limit, and a מוכר can always back out
steps.raayaSupportSource: The behavior of the תגרי לוד makes sense only if the seller's rights were not affected

steps.title: The merchants of לוד rarely made mistakes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the proof aside: the תגרי לוד rarely got their prices wrong, so a longer window for sellers was worth little to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The merchants of Lod rarely made mistakes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from steps 1 and 2. Even if the seller had the same time limit, the merchants could still have wanted a shorter one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These merchants were experts and almost never priced things wrong. So more time to back out as sellers did not help them, while more time for buyers to back out hurt them. That explains their going back without proving that a מוכר can always back out.

keyTerms.meaning: The merchants of the city of לוד
It is not common
They made a mistake (here, in setting the price)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not prove that a מוכר has the same time limit as a לוקח. It only shows that the story of the merchants cannot settle the question either way.

phrases.english: The merchants of Lod rarely make mistakes.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּגָּרֵי לוֹד לָא שְׁכִיחַ דְּטָעוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in steps 1 and 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the תגרי לוד, but does not rule on the question itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the merchants would value more time to back out as sellers. Because they rarely erred, that extra time was worth almost nothing to them.
steps.whatToRemember: The תגרי לוד story cannot decide whether a מוכר has a time limit, because these expert merchants hardly ever made pricing mistakes.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא's landlord sold a donkey too cheaply
steps.stepSummary: A story: רמי בר חמא's landlord sold a donkey at the wrong price and thought it was too late to back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא's landlord sold a donkey and made a mistake in the price. רמי בר חמא found him sad and asked why. He said he had sold a donkey and made a mistake. רמי בר חמא told him to go back out of the sale. The landlord said he had already waited longer than the time it takes to show the item to a merchant or a relative.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up a real ruling on our question. The landlord assumes a seller also has the short time limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a seller was the one who lost money, and he waited past the window given to a buyer. The landlord thought that window applied to him too. רמי בר חמא told him to back out anyway, which shows a question that now needs a ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: His landlord (the person he stayed with)
A donkey
Sad
Back out (of the sale)
The time it takes to show the item to a merchant or a relative (the time limit for backing out)

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama's landlord
sold a donkey and made a mistake.
He found him sad,
and said to him: Why are you sad?
He said to him: I sold a donkey and made a mistake.
He said to him: Go back out of the sale.
He said to him: But I have waited
longer than the time it takes to show it
to a merchant or to my relative!
phrases.notes: This is the time limit from the משנה for backing out of an unfair sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוּשְׁפִּיזְכָנֵיהּ דְּרָמֵי בַּר חָמָא זַבֵּין חֲמָרָא וּטְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof was rejected, the גמרא brings a real case that will settle the question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The story raises a case of a seller who waited past the buyer's time limit.

steps.title: רב נחמן rules that a seller may always back out
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the time limit applies only to a לוקח, and a מוכר may always back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא sent him to רב נחמן, who said: They taught this only about a buyer, but a seller can always back out.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a clear ruling from רב נחמן that answers the question of the סוגיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The short window in the משנה was set only for a לוקח. A מוכר who was overcharged may back out at any time. That is exactly what the תגרי לוד proof tried to show and could not.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent him
They taught this only about
He can always back out

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן, only a לוקח is limited to the time it takes to show the item to a merchant or relative. A מוכר who lost money from אונאה can always back out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical law: the seller's right to back out has no time limit.

phrases.english: He sent him before Rav Naḥman,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לוֹקֵחַ,
phrases.english: who said to him: They taught this only about a buyer,
but a seller can always back out.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לוֹקֵחַ, אֲבָל מוֹכֵר לְעוֹלָם חוֹזֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the case described in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A מוכר may always back out of a sale with אונאה; the time limit applies only to a לוקח.

steps.title: Why the seller gets more time than the buyer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a מוכר may always back out. It answers that a לוקח holds the item and can quickly find out its value, while a מוכר has to wait until a similar item comes his way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? A buyer has the item in his hand. Wherever he goes he can show it, and people tell him whether he made a mistake. A seller no longer has the item, so he only finds out when a similar item happens to come his way. Only then does he know whether he made a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב נחמן's ruling (step 5) and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is about how easily each side can find out the true price. The לוקח can show the item to anyone right away, so a short time is enough for him. The מוכר has given the item away and has to wait for a similar one to show up, so he cannot be held to the same short time.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
His item is in his hand
He made a mistake (about the price)
Happens to come along by chance

steps.whatToRemember: A לוקח can check the price quickly because he holds the item. A מוכר cannot, so he can always back out.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
A buyer has his merchandise in his hand,
wherever he goes he shows it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לֵיהּ אִי טְעָה, אִי לָא טְעָה.
phrases.english: and they tell him whether he erred or did not err.
A seller, who does not hold his merchandise in his hand,
has to wait until merchandise like his merchandise happens to come his way,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָדַע אִי טְעָה וְאִי לָא טְעָה.
phrases.english: and then he knows whether he erred or did not err.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? לוֹקֵחַ מִקָּחוֹ בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רב נחמן's ruling in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a מוכר is not limited by the time a לוקח has.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The לוקח can check the price at once because he holds the item. The מוכר must wait for a similar item to appear.

steps.title: The silk seller and the clever buyer
steps.stepSummary: A man asked six for silk worth five and would have taken five and a half. A buyer paid the full six on purpose so that he could sue for אונאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man had silk strips to sell. He asked six, they were worth five, and he would have accepted five and a half. A buyer said: If I pay five and a half, that counts as giving up my claim. I will pay six and then take him to court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. It sets up a question that רבא will rule on in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer is playing the rules. Paying five and a half means an overcharge of less than a שתות, which counts as מחילה and cannot be claimed back. By paying six he makes the overcharge big enough to sue for.

keyTerms.meaning: Silk strips
Giving up a claim; forgiving the overcharge
I will sue him in court

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דַּהֲוָה נָקֵט וַרְשְׁכֵי לְזַבּוֹנֵי,
phrases.english: There was a certain man who had silk strips to sell.
He called out six, and they were worth five,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי הֲווֹ יָהֲבִי לֵיהּ חַמְשָׁא וּפַלְגָא הֲוָה שָׁקֵיל.
phrases.english: and if they had given him five and a half, he would have taken it.
A certain man came and said:
phrases.notes: This is a different man: a buyer, thinking to himself.

phrases.aramaic: אִי יָהֵיבְנָא לֵיהּ חַמְשָׁא וּפַלְגָא הָוְיָא מְחִילָה.
phrases.english: If I give him five and a half, it is a waiver.
phrases.notes: Overpaying by half on five is less than a sixth, and an overcharge that small is simply forgiven.

phrases.english: I will give him six and sue him in court.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דַּהֲוָה נָקֵט וַרְשְׁכֵי לְזַבּוֹנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a case about claiming אונאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: a buyer overpays on purpose so he can claim אונאה.

steps.title: רבא: no אונאה when buying from a homeowner
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the laws of אונאה apply only when buying from a תגר, not from a בעל הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case came before רבא. He said: The rule was taught only about someone who buys from a merchant. Someone who buys from a homeowner has no claim of אונאה against him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rules on the silk case, and the buyer loses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא limits the laws of אונאה to buying from a תגר. The silk seller was a private בעל הבית, so the buyer's trick does not work. He cannot get the extra money back.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught (this law) about…
A merchant; a professional seller
A homeowner; a private person, not a merchant
Overcharging; a price that is unfairly high or low

phrases.english: It came before Rava; he said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּלוֹקֵחַ מִן הַתַּגָּר,
phrases.english: They taught this only about one who buys from a merchant,
but one who buys from a homeowner
has no claim of exploitation against him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּלוֹקֵחַ מִן הַתַּגָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the story in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אונאה applies to buying from a תגר, not from a בעל הבית.

steps.title: The jewelry seller and the same trick
steps.stepSummary: A second story: jewelry asked at sixty, worth fifty, and the seller would have taken fifty-five. A buyer pays sixty on purpose so he can sue.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man had jewelry to sell. He asked sixty, it was worth fifty, and he would have accepted fifty-five. A buyer said: If I pay fifty-five, that counts as giving up my claim. I will pay sixty and then take him to court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story that matches the first one. It sets up רב חסדא's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same trick with bigger numbers. It shows that a second אמורא faced the same kind of case on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: Jewelry (beads, ornaments)

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דַּהֲוָה נָקֵיט כִּיפֵּי לְזַבּוֹנֵי
phrases.english: There was a certain man who had jewelry to sell.
He called out sixty, and it was worth fifty,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי הֲווֹ יָהֲבִי לֵיהּ חַמְשִׁין וְחַמְשָׁא הֲוָה שָׁקֵיל.
phrases.english: and if they had given him fifty-five, he would have taken it.
A certain man came and said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי יָהֵיבְנָא לֵיהּ חַמְשִׁין וְחַמְשָׁא הָוְיָא מְחִילָה,
phrases.english: If I give him fifty-five, it is a waiver;
I will give him sixty and sue him in court.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דַּהֲוָה נָקֵיט כִּיפֵּי לְזַבּוֹנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case that matches the silk story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up a second case of overpaying on purpose to claim אונאה.

steps.title: רב חסדא gives the same ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules just like רבא: buying from a בעל הבית gives no claim of אונאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case came before רב חסדא. He said: The rule was taught only about someone who buys from a merchant. Someone who buys from a homeowner has no claim of אונאה against him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא rules on the jewelry case, using the same words as רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now two אמוראים hold the same rule, so it is not one person's opinion. רב חסדא's ruling is the one that gets challenged in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who ruled on the jewelry case

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: It came before Rav Chisda. He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּלוֹקֵחַ מִן הַתַּגָּר,
phrases.english: They taught this only about one who buys from a merchant,
but one who buys from a homeowner
has no claim of exploitation against him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the story in step 9, matching רבא in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No אונאה when buying from a בעל הבית.

steps.title: Two sages approve the ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי tells רב חסדא his ruling is right, and רבי אלעזר also said it was right.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי said to him: Well said. And רבי אלעזר also said: Well said.
steps.whatsHappening: Two more sages agree with רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The approval from רב דימי, and from רבי אלעזר, an אמורא of ארץ ישראל, makes the rule stronger. This makes the question in the next step sharper.

keyTerms.meaning: Well said! (literally: may your strength be firm)
And so too said…

phrases.english: Rav Dimi said to him: Well said.
And likewise Rabbi Elazar said: Well said.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב דִּימִי: יִשַׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's ruling that buying from a בעל הבית gives no claim of אונאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The agreement of רב דימי and רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: A משנה says אונאה applies to a regular person too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: אונאה applies to a הדיוט just as it does to a תגר. A הדיוט sounds like a בעל הבית, which goes against the ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: Just as אונאה applies to a regular person, so it applies to a merchant. Who is the 'regular person'? Isn't it a homeowner?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא and רב חסדא with a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה puts the הדיוט and the תגר side by side and says אונאה applies to both. If הדיוט means a private בעל הבית, then the משנה says the laws of אונאה apply to him. That goes against what רבא and רב חסדא ruled.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)?
A regular person, not a professional
Isn't it…? (a question that expects 'yes')

steps.confusionAlert: Here the גמרא assumes הדיוט means a private homeowner. In the next step רב חסדא does not deny this. He explains that the משנה is talking about a different kind of item.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאוֹנָאָה לְהֶדְיוֹט כָּךְ אוֹנָאָה לַתַּגָּר.
phrases.english: Just as exploitation applies to a layman, so exploitation applies to a merchant.
Who is the layman? Is it not a homeowner?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling that steps 10 and 11 just backed up.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that buying from a בעל הבית gives no claim of אונאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says אונאה applies to a הדיוט, and a הדיוט seems to be a בעל הבית.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the משנה is about simple linen goods
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the משנה is about simple linen garments made to be sold. When a בעל הבית sells his own personal things, which he cares about, he only sells them for extra money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The משנה is about simple linen garments. But his personal items, which are precious to him, he only sells for extra money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the challenge by dividing between two kinds of items a בעל הבית might sell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בעל הבית selling plain goods made to be sold is like any seller, so אונאה applies, just as the משנה says. When he sells his own personal things, everyone knows he asks a high price because they matter to him. So the buyer knowingly accepted a higher price and has no claim of אונאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Simple linen garments, made to be sold
His personal items, things he uses himself
Precious to him
Extra money; a higher price

steps.whatToRemember: A בעל הבית selling his own personal belongings is not held to the laws of אונאה, because buyers know he charges extra for things he cares about. Plain goods made for sale still follow the regular laws of אונאה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer turns on what kind of item is sold, not only on who sells it. It also explains why buyers in the two stories had no claim.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: It is about simple linen garments.
But his personal-use items, which are precious to him,

phrases.aramaic: לָא מְזַבֵּין לְהוּ אִי לָאו בִּדְמֵי יַתִּירֵי.
phrases.english: he does not sell them except for extra money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בְּצַדְרְיָיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to one kind of item
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say that all sales by a בעל הבית follow the laws of אונאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is only about simple goods made for sale. A בעל הבית's personal items are sold for extra money, so there is no אונאה.

steps.title: New משנה: Overcharging Goes Both Ways and Applies to Merchants
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that אונאה applies to buyer and seller alike, and to a הדיוט and a תגר alike. רבי יהודה disagrees about the תגר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Both the buyer and the seller are covered by the laws of overcharging. Overcharging applies to a merchant just as it applies to a regular person. רבי יהודה says: there is no overcharging for a merchant.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with the basic rules of who is covered by אונאה. This is the same משנה line that was quoted against רב חסדא back in Step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate points here. First, the rule goes both ways: a seller can be cheated by a buyer, not only the other way around. Second, a professional תגר is covered just like a regular person, except according to רבי יהודה, who says a תגר has no claim of אונאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה being studied
Buyer
Seller
A regular person, not a professional
A merchant, a trader

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Both the buyer and the seller
are covered by the laws of overcharging.
Just as overcharging applies to a regular person,
so overcharging applies to a merchant.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
There is no overcharging for a merchant.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד הַלּוֹקֵחַ וְאֶחָד הַמּוֹכֵר יֵשׁ לָהֶן אוֹנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. Its line about הדיוט and תגר is the one quoted as a challenge in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אונאה applies to both buyer and seller, and to both a הדיוט and a תגר. רבי יהודה exempts the תגר.

steps.title: The Cheated Side Chooses: Cancel or Get the Difference
steps.stepSummary: The person who was cheated has the upper hand. He may cancel the sale or demand back the amount he was overcharged.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who was cheated has the upper hand. If he wants, he can say: give me back my money. Or he can say: give me back the amount you overcharged me.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now says what happens after someone was cheated. The cheated side gets to pick the remedy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cheater has no say in the matter. The victim chooses between two options. He can undo the whole sale and get his money back, or he can keep the deal and get back only the overcharge.

keyTerms.meaning: It was put upon him, meaning he is the one who was cheated
His hand is on top; he has the upper hand
My money

steps.whatToRemember: In this משנה, אונאה goes both ways and covers merchants too (except for רבי יהודה). The cheated person chooses: cancel the sale or get the difference back.

phrases.english: The one on whom it was imposed
phrases.notes: He means the one the overcharging was done to, the victim.

phrases.english: has the upper hand.
If he wants, he says to him:
Give me back my money,
or give me what you overcharged me.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁהוּטַּל עָלָיו יָדוֹ עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה. It moves from who is covered to what the remedy is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cheated party chooses between cancelling the sale and getting back the overcharge.

steps.title: גמרא Asks for the Source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that אונאה applies to both buyer and seller.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's first rule. It is setting up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the opening line of the משנה: that both the buyer and the seller are covered. The גמרא wants to see where the Torah teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
From where do we know these things?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the Torah source of the משנה's rule in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches אונאה protects both buyer and seller.

steps.title: The Verse Covers Both the Buyer and the Seller
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns that a cheated buyer is protected from the words 'if you sell,' and that a cheated seller is protected from the words 'or buy.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'And if you sell something to your fellow... do not overcharge.' This only teaches about a buyer who was cheated. From where do we know a seller who was cheated is also covered? The פסוק says: 'or buy... do not overcharge.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. Each half of the פסוק protects a different side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'If you sell' warns the seller, so it protects the buyer. 'Or buy' warns the buyer, so it protects the seller. Since the same פסוק mentions both, both sides are covered.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this introduces a ברייתא
Do not overcharge (or cheat)
The verse teaches
Was overcharged, was cheated

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"And if you sell something to your fellow...
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:14. The dots mean the גמרא skipped the middle words of the פסוק.

phrases.english: do not overcharge"
I only know about a case where the buyer was cheated;
where the seller was cheated, from where do we know?
The verse teaches:
"or buy... do not overcharge."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן וְכִי תִמְכְּרוּ מִמְכָּר לַעֲמִיתֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 25:14: 'if you sell' covers a cheated buyer, and 'or buy' covers a cheated seller.

steps.title: Why Writing Only the Seller Would Not Be Enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a צריכא, explaining why the Torah had to write both. If it had warned only the seller, we might say he is warned because he knows the value, but a buyer who does not know the value is not warned.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to write the buyer and necessary to write the seller. If the Torah had written only the seller, I would say he is warned because he knows what his merchandise is worth. But a buyer does not know what the merchandise is worth, so I would say the Torah did not warn him with 'do not overcharge.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining why the Torah needed both halves of the פסוק. This step gives the first half of the reasoning; the second half comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A seller knows the real price, so cheating looks fully on purpose and deserves a warning. A buyer usually does not know the price, so we might think the Torah would not hold him to the same warning. That is why the Torah wrote the buyer separately.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
He is sure, he knows clearly
His merchandise
Warned him, forbade him

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the direction. In the ברייתא, 'the seller was cheated' means the seller is the victim. Here, 'if the Torah wrote the seller' means the seller is the one being warned not to cheat.

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write the buyer
and it was necessary to write the seller,
for if the Merciful One had written only the seller,
I would say that is because he knows what his merchandise is worth,
but a buyer,
who does not know what the merchandise is worth,
I would say the Merciful One did not warn him
with "do not overcharge."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִכְתַּב לוֹקֵחַ וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִכְתַּב מוֹכֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ברייתא's two-part learning is needed. It shows the seller's warning could not teach the buyer's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seller's warning cannot teach the buyer's, because the seller knows the value and the buyer does not.

steps.title: Why Writing Only the Buyer Would Not Be Enough, So Both Are Needed
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah had warned only the buyer, we might say he is warned because buying is a gain, but a seller who is losing his item is not warned. So both had to be written.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Torah had written only the buyer, I would say he is warned because he is gaining something, as people say: 'You bought, you gained.' But a seller is losing out, as people say: 'He sold, he lost.' So I would say the Torah did not warn him with 'do not overcharge.' Therefore both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the reasoning from the other side. It concludes that the Torah had to write both the buyer and the seller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A buyer comes out ahead, so it makes sense to warn him not to cheat as well. A seller is giving up his item, so we might have gone easy on him. Since neither case could be learned from the other, the Torah wrote both.

keyTerms.meaning: People say; a common saying
You bought, you gained
He sold, he lost
It is necessary; both verses are needed

steps.whatToRemember: The Torah warns both buyer and seller not to cheat. Neither could be learned from the other: the seller knows the value, and the buyer gains from the deal. That is why the Torah needed to write both.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only the buyer,
I would say that is because he is acquiring something,
as people say:
"You bought, you gained."
But a seller, who is losing out,
as people say:
"He sold, he lost,"
I would say the Merciful One did not warn him
with "do not overcharge."
Therefore both are necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא לוֹקֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכא begun in Step 18 by arguing from the other side.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both the buyer's warning and the seller's warning are needed, because each has a reason that could not be learned from the other.

steps.title: How can being a merchant remove protection from overcharging?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's ruling that a merchant has no אונאה and asks in surprise why being a merchant should change anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבי יהודה says a merchant has no אונאה. The גמרא asks: just because he is a merchant, he loses the protection of אונאה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה, רבי יהודה's ruling about a merchant, and immediately questions it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anyone, even a merchant, can make a mistake about a price. So why should a merchant be left unprotected when he is cheated? The גמרא wants a reason for רבי יהודה's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A merchant, someone who buys and sells for a living
Overcharging or underpaying in a sale, which the Torah forbids
Just because he is...

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
There is no overcharging protection for a merchant.
Just because he is a merchant
he has no protection from overcharging?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם שֶׁהוּא תַּגָּר אֵין לוֹ אוֹנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic in the משנה after finishing the צריכא about buyer and seller.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that a merchant has no אונאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being a merchant does not stop someone from making a pricing mistake, so there seems to be no reason to take away his protection.

steps.title: A professional trader knows his prices and gave up the difference
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רב explains that רבי יהודה means a professional trader. He knows the true value, so he must have forgiven the difference, probably because he needed cash for another deal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רב: they taught this about a trader who buys and sells. Why? He surely knows what his merchandise is worth, and he gave up the difference to the buyer. He sold it this way because another deal came his way and he needed the money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question by limiting רבי יהודה's rule to a professional trader and giving the reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A trader cannot claim he did not know the price. So if he sold too cheaply, we assume he did it on purpose and forgave the difference. The reason he would do that is that he wanted quick money for another good opportunity.

keyTerms.meaning: A trader or dealer who buys goods to resell them
He surely forgave or gave up (the money)
Merchandise, or a deal
It happened to come his way

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rav:
They taught this about a merchant who is a trader.
What is the reason?
He surely knows how much his merchandise is worth,
and he forgave the difference to the buyer.
And the reason he sold it this way
is because there came his way
another deal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַב: בְּתַגָּר סַפְסָר שָׁנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 by defining which merchant is meant and why.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) and giving a reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any merchant loses protection just for being a merchant, which makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a professional trader, who knows prices, loses it, because he must have forgiven the difference.

steps.title: But the merchant is trying to back out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן: the merchant in our case wants to cancel the sale, which shows he did not forgive anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: But right now, in any case, he is backing out of the sale!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן's explanation from the facts of the case itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said we assume the trader forgave the difference. But a person who forgave would not come back to complain. His trying to back out proves he did not forgive.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, in any case
He backs out, he goes back on the deal

phrases.english: But now, in any case,
he is backing out of the deal!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא מִיהָא קָא הָדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given by רב נחמן in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that the trader forgave the difference
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone who forgave would not try to cancel the sale, so his complaint shows he never forgave.

steps.title: רב אשי: a merchant can back out even for a small difference
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reads רבי יהודה the opposite way: a merchant is not bound by the normal rules of אונאה, so he may back out even when he was cheated by less than the usual amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: what does 'a merchant has no אונאה' mean? He is not held to the normal rules of אונאה, because he may back out even for less than the amount that normally counts as אונאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different reading of רבי יהודה's words that avoids the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of 'no protection,' רב אשי reads 'not bound by the usual measure.' Normally a gap of less than a sixth is simply forgiven, but a merchant may back out even over a gap that small. That fits the fact that he is trying to cancel the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: Under the normal rules of אונאה
Less than the amount that counts as אונאה (less than a sixth)
He can back out of the sale

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי turns רבי יהודה's ruling upside down. 'אין לתגר אונאה' does not mean the merchant has less protection. It means he has more: the usual one-sixth limit does not apply to him.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
What does 'a merchant has no אונאה' mean?
He is not under the normal rules of אונאה,
since even for less than the amount of אונאה
phrases.notes: Normally the cheating has to reach a sixth of the price before it counts as אונאה.

phrases.english: he may back out.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מַאי אֵין לַתַּגָּר אוֹנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 by offering a new reading of רבי יהודה instead of defending רב נחמן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the words of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'No אונאה' means the merchant has no protection, which clashes with his trying to back out.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'No אונאה' means he is free of the usual limits and may back out even for less than a sixth.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying a merchant has no אונאה because he is an expert, which matches רב נחמן's reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches like רב נחמן: רבי יהודה says a merchant has no אונאה, because he is an expert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב נחמן's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the reason 'because he is an expert.' That is exactly רב נחמן's point: the merchant knows prices, so he must have given up the difference. This supports רב נחמן over רב אשי's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught in line with his view
An expert, someone who knows the field well

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of 'אין לתגר אונאה.' רב נחמן: a trader knows prices, so he forgave the difference and cannot complain. רב אשי: a merchant can back out even for less than a sixth. The ברייתא's words 'because he is an expert' support רב נחמן.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא like Rav Nachman:
Rabbi Yehuda says,
a merchant has no אונאה protection,
because he is an expert.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רב נחמן's explanation (step 21) after רב אשי's alternative (step 23).
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's explanation that a trader knows the value and forgave the difference
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יהודה gives the reason 'because he is an expert'

steps.title: Whose opinion is the rule that the cheated person has the upper hand?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that the cheated person has the upper hand and asks which תנא it follows. It answers that it is neither רבי נתן nor רבי יהודה הנשיא, setting up an explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: the one who was cheated has the upper hand, and so on. Whose opinion is our משנה? It is not רבי נתן and not רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier line of the משנה to ask whose view it follows. This step sets up the next move, where the גמרא will explain the views of רבי נתן and רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets the cheated person choose: cancel the sale or get back the overcharge. The גמרא claims this choice does not match either רבי נתן or רבי יהודה הנשיא. It has not yet shown why; that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The one on whom (the cheating) was placed, the person who was cheated
He has the upper hand, he gets to choose
Whose opinion is our משנה?

phrases.english: The one on whom the cheating was placed
phrases.notes: This is the line from the משנה we saw back in step 15.

phrases.english: has the upper hand, and so on.
Whose opinion is our משנה?
Not Rabbi Natan
and not Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי מַתְנִיתִין? לָא רַבִּי נָתָן וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the merchant topic and returns to the משנה's earlier rule from step 15 to identify its author.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's opinion matches the משנה's rule that the cheated person may choose to cancel or recover the overcharge.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גמרא says it is neither רבי נתן nor רבי יהודה הנשיא. Step 26 explains why, and steps 28-30 resolve the problem.

steps.title: Why the משנה fits neither רבי נתן nor רבי יהודה הנשיא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the mismatch between the משנה and each of the two ברייתא opinions.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה follows רבי נתן, there is a problem: the משנה says 'if he wishes,' but רבי נתן in the ברייתא does not say 'if he wishes.' If it follows רבי יהודה הנשיא, there is also a problem: the משנה talks about the buyer, but רבי יהודה הנשיא in the ברייתא talks about the seller.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains its claim from the last step that the משנה matches neither תנא. It points to one clear difference with each of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the cheated person a choice ('if he wishes'), but רבי נתן's ברייתא has no choice in it. With רבי יהודה הנשיא the problem is different: the משנה gives the advantage to the buyer, while his ברייתא gives it to the seller. So each match breaks on a different detail.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If he wishes': the cheated person gets to choose
A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה
The buyer
The seller

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different problems here, one for each תנא. The רבי נתן problem is about the word 'רצה' (having a choice). The רבי יהודה הנשיא problem is about buyer versus seller.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Natan —
the Mishnah teaches "if he wishes,"
but the baraita does not teach "if he wishes."
If it is Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi —
the Mishnah teaches about the "buyer,"
but the baraita teaches about the "seller."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי נָתָן – מַתְנִיתִין קָתָנֵי ״רָצָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the difficulty claimed in step 25: each possible author clashes with the משנה on a different detail. Steps 27-29 respond to this difficulty.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה cannot follow רבי נתן or רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With רבי נתן the 'רצה' choice is missing, and with רבי יהודה הנשיא the seller appears instead of the buyer.
steps.kashyaTarget: Attributing the משנה's rule (the cheated party has the upper hand and may choose) to either רבי נתן or רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי נתן's ברייתא lacks the 'רצה' choice found in the משנה, and רבי יהודה הנשיא's ברייתא gives the advantage to the seller while the משנה speaks of the buyer. So neither תנא fits.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר admits he does not know who taught it
steps.stepSummary: After a memory aid listing the coming speakers, רבי אלעזר says he cannot identify the תנא of this משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: Z-B-R-Sh.) רבי אלעזר said: I do not know who taught this law of אונאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first gives a short memory aid for the four אמוראים who will speak. Then רבי אלעזר simply accepts the problem and says he does not know whose opinion the משנה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר does not try to fix the problem from step 26. He leaves the משנה without a known author. The next two אמוראים will each try to solve it.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid that helps you remember the order of the speakers
Taught it

phrases.english: (Memory aid: Z-B-R-Sh)
phrases.notes: The letters stand for the speakers coming up: רבי אלעזר, רבה, רבא, and רב אשי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
This law of overcharging,
I do not know who taught it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אוֹנָאָה זוֹ אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מִי שְׁנָאָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the problem raised in step 26 without solving it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The author of the משנה's אונאה law cannot be identified.

steps.title: רבה: it is רבי נתן, and the ברייתא's wording is fixed
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the משנה follows רבי נתן, and adds 'רצה' to the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Really it is רבי נתן, and also read 'if he wishes' in the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה solves the רבי נתן problem by changing the wording of the ברייתא so that it also says 'if he wishes.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only problem with רבי נתן was the missing word 'רצה.' רבה says the ברייתא should include it too. Once it does, the משנה and רבי נתן say the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Really' or 'actually': I am sticking with the first idea after all
'And read': fix the wording of the text this way

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Actually, it is Rabbi Natan,
and read "if he wishes" in the baraita as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי נָתָן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבי נתן half of the problem in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Fixing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי נתן gives no choice, so he cannot be the author of the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא also says 'רצה,' so רבי נתן matches the משנה.

steps.title: רבא: it is רבי יהודה הנשיא, and the two sources complete each other
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה follows רבי יהודה הנשיא. The משנה left out the seller, and the ברייתא fills that in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really it is רבי יהודה הנשיא. What he left out in the משנה, he explains in the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא solves the רבי יהודה הנשיא problem without changing any text. He says the משנה and the ברייתא each cover a different part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was buyer versus seller. רבא says there is no argument here: the משנה spoke about the buyer and left the seller out, and the ברייתא adds the seller. Both have the upper hand.

keyTerms.meaning: Left out (but did not reject)
Explains, spells out

phrases.english: Rava said:
Actually, it is Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi,
and what he left out in the Mishnah
he explains in the baraita.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different solution from רבה's, this time for the רבי יהודה הנשיא half of the problem.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two sources complete each other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה (buyer) and the ברייתא (seller) seem to disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה left out the seller, and the ברייתא adds him. Both buyer and seller have the upper hand.

steps.title: רב אשי supports רבא from the משנה's wording
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens with 'both buyer and seller' but only explains the buyer, which shows the seller was just left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The wording supports this too. The משנה says 'both the buyer and the seller,' but then explains only the buyer. Learn from this that it simply left out the seller. The גמרא agrees: learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings proof for רבא from the משנה's own words. The גמרא then accepts the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה opens by naming both the buyer and the seller, so the seller is clearly included. Since it then spells out only the buyer's case, the seller's case must have been left out, not rejected. This is exactly what רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The wording supports this too': a proof from how the text is written
Both the buyer and the seller
'Learn from it': the point is proven

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer: the משנה follows רבי יהודה הנשיא. The משנה and the ברייתא complete each other, so both the cheated buyer and the cheated seller have the upper hand.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The wording is precise as well,
since it teaches "both the buyer and the seller,"
and then explains only the buyer;
learn from this
that it simply left out the seller.
Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: דַּיְקָא נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's answer in step 29.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the משנה left out the seller without rejecting him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's opening words 'אחד הלוקח ואחד המוכר.'

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about a sale with a 'no overcharge claim' condition
steps.stepSummary: Someone sells on condition that the other side has no אונאה claim. רב says the claim still stands, and שמואל says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If someone tells his friend, 'on condition that you have no אונאה claim against me,' רב says he still has an אונאה claim against him. שמואל says he has no אונאה claim against him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב and שמואל argue about whether a condition can cancel a person's right to claim אונאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a person who is overcharged can claim the difference back. Here both sides agreed ahead of time that there would be no such claim. רב says the condition does not work, and שמואל says it does.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was stated': introduces an argument between אמוראים
On condition that
Overcharging or underpaying, which gives the cheated side a claim

phrases.english: It was stated:
One who says to his fellow:

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֵין לְךָ עָלַי אוֹנָאָה.
phrases.english: "On condition that you have no overcharge claim against me."
Rav says:
He does have an overcharge claim against him.
And Shmuel says:
He has no overcharge claim against him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֵין לְךָ עָלַי אוֹנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the question of which תנא the משנה follows was settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the condition does not cancel the אונאה claim. שמואל: it does cancel it.

steps.title: Suggestion that רב follows רבי מאיר and שמואל follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the argument between רב and שמואל is the same as an earlier argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב holds like רבי מאיר, and שמואל holds like רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that this argument is really an older argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will test the suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לימא' brings a suggestion, not a final ruling. If it holds, רב and שמואל would each just be following a תנא. The גמרא usually tries to push back on a 'לימא' suggestion.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall we say': a suggestion the גמרא will now test

phrases.english: Shall we say
that Rav spoke in line with Rabbi Meir,
and Shmuel spoke in line with Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַב דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to tie the רב–שמואל argument from step 31 to an earlier argument between תנאים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב and שמואל are simply following רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The ברייתא about betrothal with a condition to give up the wife's rights
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא it is comparing to. רבי מאיר says a condition against a Torah money right does not work, and רבי יהודה says it does work in money matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: A man says to a woman, 'You are betrothed to me on condition that you have no claim on me for food, clothing, and marital relations.' She is betrothed, and his condition does not count. This is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יהודה says: in money matters, his condition stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for its suggestion from the last step. It quotes a ברייתא where רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about a condition that cancels a wife's rights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds you cannot make a condition against what the Torah requires, so the condition fails. רבי יהודה says money rights, like food and clothing, can be given up by condition. The suggestion is that רב follows רבי מאיר (the אונאה claim stays) and שמואל follows רבי יהודה (the condition works).

keyTerms.meaning: Food, clothing, and marital relations, which a husband owes his wife
On condition that
His condition does not count
A money matter
His condition stands and works

steps.confusionAlert: Both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה agree the woman is betrothed. They only argue about whether the condition works.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: One who says to a woman:
You are hereby betrothed to me
on condition that you have no claim against me
phrases.notes: The word for 'you' here has a masculine form, but he is talking to the woman.

phrases.english: for food, clothing, and marital relations –
she is betrothed,
and his condition is void; these are the words of רבי מאיר.
רבי יהודה says:
In a money matter – his condition stands.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא that the suggestion in step 32 depends on.
steps.raayaObject: The suggestion that רב follows רבי מאיר and שמואל follows רבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about קידושין on condition the wife gives up שאר כסות ועונה
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the base case for the whole question of whether a condition can cancel a money right the Torah gives.

steps.title: רב can agree even with רבי יהודה because the wife knew what she gave up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to reject the comparison. רב can say his view fits even רבי יהודה, because רבי יהודה only allows the condition where the woman knows her rights and gives them up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב could tell you: I said my view even according to רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה only said his view there, because she knows and gives it up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to push back on the idea that רב must follow רבי מאיר. This sets up a difference between the two cases, and the other half of that difference comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the betrothal case, the woman knows exactly what rights she is giving up, so she truly waives them. That is why רבי יהודה lets the condition stand. רב is setting up a contrast with the אונאה case, and the second half of that contrast comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (the גמרא answers for someone)
He only said his view up to here, meaning only in that case
She knows
She gives up or forgives her right

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not arguing with רבי יהודה. He is saying רבי יהודה's rule only covers a case where the person knows what she is giving up.

phrases.english: רב could say to you:
I stated my view even according to רבי יהודה –

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָתָם,
phrases.english: רבי יהודה only stated his view there,
because she knows and is giving it up,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison in steps 32-33 by pointing to a difference between the betrothal case and the אונאה case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only rejects the claim that רב must follow רבי מאיר. It does not reject רבי יהודה's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison misses that in the betrothal case the woman knowingly gives up her rights. In the אונאה case that may not be true.
